text:
ada: Heads-up — Prospect (Orpheus Health) wants Redwood as a drop-in for their current vendor (HeliosAPI). Minimal client changes, same request/response shapes, and a short security checklist due Friday. Can we POC?
liam: Yes, feasible. Main compatibility items: top-level field names (`context` vs `input/messages`), streaming framing (chunked JSON vs SSE), webhook callbacks, and legacy error codes.
mira: +1. Also they use `dedupe_key` and expect `409` for duplicates. We'll need an idempotency mapping.
sahil: Security: they are healthcare. Need BAA, KMS details, audit log retention options, and mTLS for certain management endpoints. I'll take the questionnaire.
ada: (ops-bot) Reminder: hosted infra cannot accept customer-supplied long-lived tokens. Use auth-proxy pattern for Hosted; Dedicated can do customer tokens/mTLS.
liam: Plan proposal: 1) lightweight compatibility proxy that accepts Helios endpoints, translates payloads/headers, and maps errors. 2) parity run on N=100 canonical clinical notes (customer to provide). 3) 30-day pilot with routing fallback if drift > threshold. 4) pricing: pilot credit or short-term blended rate.
mira: Need sample cURL and example webhook shape. Also confirm whether customer needs stream framing exactly identical — they said yes for older clients.
ada: Customer sample (redacted):

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer HELIOS_TOKEN" \n  -d '{"context":"Patient note...","max_length":400,"callback_url":"https://orp/cb","dedupe_key":"abc-1"}' \n  https://api.helios.ai/v2/complete

Expected async callback: POST /cb with body: {"job_id":"j-1","status":"finished","result":{"summary":"..."},"meta":{"request_id":"r-1"}}

liam: Quick shim sketch (node/express):

// POST /v2/complete -> map to Redwood
app.post('/v2/complete', async (req, res) => {
  const helios = req.body;
  const redwoodBody = { input: helios.context, max_tokens: helios.max_length };
  // call Redwood API, handle streaming -> chunked JSON transform, then return/maybe POST to callback_url
});

mira: Important: Helios does a PHI post-process filter that can alter outputs. We can emulate but must set expectation: best-effort parity, acceptance via agreed QA tests.
sahil: Ops question: can we accept their Helios tokens in Hosted for the pilot? Short answer: no. We'll provide an auth-proxy that validates their token and mints ephemeral Redwood tokens; logs mapping for audit. Dedicated could accept their tokens if they manage the key.
liam: For error mapping: map Redwood validation -> 422, duplicate -> 409, and preserve `X-Helios-Limit` headers (synthesize if needed).
mira: ETA for prototype shim: 2 business days if I get cURL samples and webhook secret.
liam: I'll run the eval harness once we have 100 examples. Suggest initial smoke N=20 this week to surface big gaps.
ada: deploy-bot: deploy started by mira for branch shim/orpheus-compat at commit 7f1a2 - staging proxy: https://staging-proxy.redwood.net/helios/v2/complete
mira: Staging up. Sync flow OK. Streaming wrapper needs final EOF frame to match Helios clients.
sahil: I'll draft questionnaire answers and BAA options. Also note retention: they asked about 7 years for audit logs — that's an enterprise add-on.
ada: ops-bot: Uploaded presales folder: https://redwood-internal/company/orpheus/presales
liam: Pricing note: propose a pilot credit equal to X% of expected spend rather than a long-term unit price change. Finance needs to weigh in.
mira: Action items: mira -> shim prototype and staging endpoint, liam -> eval harness runs and metrics, sahil -> questionnaire/BAA + retention options, ada -> SOW + pricing ask to finance.
ada: follow-ups next week unless customer pushes earlier. :thumbsup:
